newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad puts back legislative elections to December.
newsitem.headline: Chad puts back legislative elections to December.

text.p: Chad has put back by a month parliamentary elections scheduled to start on November 24 to wrap up a transition to democracy in the Central African country, an official announcement said on Wednesday.
The Independent National Electoral Commission published a new timetable setting the first round of voting for December 22 with a second round ballot on February 2, 1997.
It gave no explanation for the changes.
Under the new timetable, final results are expected on February 23, with the 125-member parliament scheduled to be installed on March 10.
The registration of nominations with the commission opened on Wednesday, to close on October 23. Campaigning for the first round runs from November 27 to December 18.

Chad's faltering transition marked its most important stage last July when former warlord and guerrilla leader Idriss Deby won presidential elections and a mandate to continue in office. He took 69 percent of votes in the second round on July 3, outpolling southern rival Wadal Adelkader Kamougue.
Deby, a northerner, seized power in 1990 in a French-backed coup. He legalised political parties in 1991, but the transition has lagged well behind that of other states in the region.
